title: Ukraine's Military Faces Limits on Starlink Satellite Service
summary:
Ukraine's military has lost some access to Starlink, a satellite internet system it has relied on during its war with Russia, according to Ukrainian officials.

Starlink is run by Elon Musk's company SpaceX. It uses more than 11,000 satellites in low orbit around Earth to deliver fast internet connections. A more secure military version is called Starshield. Shortly after Russia invaded Ukraine in February 2022, a Ukrainian leader asked Musk to turn Starlink on in the country, and Musk soon did.

It is not clear why the new restrictions were put in place. On Wednesday, Musk wrote on the social media site X that Starshield systems are owned and controlled by the U.S. government. He said any limits would have been ordered by the U.S. military and, in the end, the president. CBC News reported that the U.S. government had not responded so far. The restrictions come as President Donald Trump has criticized Ukraine's president, Volodymyr Zelenskyy, for attacks on Russian oil refineries, which Trump blames for high oil prices.

According to Serhii Beskrestnov, a technology adviser to Zelenskyy, Ukraine uses the network for drone missions, air defense and delivering supplies to the front line. He said the restrictions included a speed limit on Starlink equipment mounted on drones.

Experts explained why the system matters. Thomas Withington of the Royal United Services Institute called it "an incredibly capable communication system." He said it lets soldiers near the front talk with commanders hundreds of kilometers away, and that it is very hard for enemies to jam, or block. Renard Sexton, a professor at Emory University, said Starlink was crucial in helping Ukraine push back against Russia's first invasion in 2022.
why_it_matters: The story shows how a private company's technology has become important in a war, and raises questions about who controls it and why its use was limited.

keywords.explanation: A satellite is a machine sent into space to circle Earth, often to send signals.
An orbit is the curved path an object follows as it travels around a planet.
Restrictions are rules or limits that stop something from being used fully.
Refineries are factories that turn crude oil into fuels such as gasoline and diesel.
Air defense is the equipment and work used to protect an area from attacks from the sky.
To jam a signal means to block it so messages cannot get through.

background_read: Starlink is a network of many small satellites that orbit close to Earth and beam internet signals to dishes on the ground.
Because the signals come from space, Starlink can work in places where phone towers and cables have been damaged, which is why it became important during the war in Ukraine.
Russia invaded Ukraine in February 2022, and Ukraine's military has used Starlink to communicate across long distances.
Starshield is a more secure version of the network built for government and military use, and Elon Musk says it is controlled by the U.S. government.
